meta.label: Training · Men · Standard
meta.notes: The everyday men's Training A+: hero, Fabric in Focus, then 3 or 4 alternating callouts. Measured off all three men's Training designs on Page 2 — Compression Top Solid 2 (1097:1514, 707041/707042/707044), Trackpants Graphic (1097:1383, 707564/707565/707566) and Shorts Graphic 1 (1097:1633, 707175/707176/707177). Only one men's template exists because the three designs are structurally identical: same hero stack, same fabric card, same alternating callout rig, no extra block in any of them. What separates them is the accent colour (meta.artDirection) and how many features the sheet row fills, and neither is a template. THE MEN'S HERO HAS ONE PHOTO DROP, NOT TWO: training/_base.json's hero.layers carries no `model` role, so only `bgPhoto` is placed. That is the designer's decision, taken by hand on the approved frame (TEMPLATE · TRAINING · MEN · Standard, 1109:2) and reconciled into the manifest — it is NOT an oversight, and it has already been undone by mistake once. The full reasoning is in training/_base.json meta.knownDeviations. The women's hero is genuinely different and keeps its model slot.

hero.comment: Only the two photo-slot labels are men's-specific; all geometry comes from training/_base.json. `model` is overridden here for its name and label ONLY — the slot is not drawn, because _base's hero.layers has no `model` role. The override is kept so the label is already correct if the slot is ever deliberately re-enabled, and because validate.js requires hero.model to exist. Adding the role back is a design decision, not a bug fix — read meta.notes first.
